items.label: FIGURE 3.12
items.title: Positive relationship between income levels and GHG emissions (continued)
items.content: The chart is a stacked area chart showing cumulative CO2 emissions (gt) from 1850 to 2020. The x-axis represents years from 1850 to 2020. The y-axis represents cumulative CO2 emissions in gigatons (gt), ranging from 0 to 2,000. The legend includes: Low-income, Lower-middle-income, Upper-middle-income, and High-income. The chart shows that high-income and upper-middle-income countries are responsible for 90 percent of historical emissions. Sources: Emissions Database for Global Atmospheric Research, Grassi et al. 2023, and World Development Indicators (panels a and b); and PRIMAP-hist data from Gütschow, Pflüger, and Busch 2024 (panel c). Note: CO2e = carbon dioxide equivalent; GHG = greenhouse gas; LULUCF = land use, land use change, and forestry. Panel c: CO2 emissions are cumulative, in gigatons (gt), and do not include emissions from LULUCF. Panels a and c: Country income groups are fixed at 2022 definitions.
